rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING THAT THE RESPONSIBILITIE S, FUNCTIONS AND PERSONNEL OF THE DEPARTMENT OF AGRICULTURE DEVOLVED TO THE LOCAL GOVERNMENT UNITS BE REVERTED TO THE NATIONAL GOVERNMENT
rows.abstract: Rationale: The devolution of basic services and facilities of the Department of Agriculture to the Local Government Units (LGUs) under Republic Act No. 7160, has financially over-burdened the budget of the LGUs, resulting in the inefficient performance of specific functions and responsibilitie s of the LGUs. The group that suffers most as a consequence of such devolution are the personnel of the Department of Agriculture. Much to the desire of the LGUs to accommodate the devolved personnel andgive them what is due them under the law, they can give only what they can, considering their meager resources and the budgetary limitations set by the Department of Budget and Management. > This bill, therefore, seeks to revert to the national goverrnment the devolved functions and responsibilitie s as well as personnel of the Department of Agricutlure from the Local Government Units.

rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE REORGANIZATION OF THE NATIONAL POLICE COMMISSION AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: "National Police Commission Act of 2002." This proposed measure intends to reorganized the National Police Commission (Napolcom) which shall take charge of police operation relating to the public safety of the nation, administer the affairs concerning police education, police communication, criminal identification, criminal statistics, police equipment, as well as coordinate the affairs concerning police administration. The Commission shall be composed of a Chairman who shall have a rank equivalent to the Secretary of the Cabinet and four (4) regular members who shall have a salary equivalent to that of an Undersecretary. The term of office of members of the Commission shall be seven (7) years without reappointment. > The Commission shallestablish, operate and maintain regional, provincial and district offices to be headed by regional, provincial and district directors, respectively, who shall implement the policies and programs of the Commission in their respective offices.

This bill states that any unmarried pregnant woman who is in government service, or in any of its instrumentaliti es including government owned or controlled corporation, and in the private sector, irrespective of herstatus of appointment, and who has rendered an aggregate service of at least six (6) months, shall be entitled to a maternity leave of at least two (2) weeks prior to the expected date of delivery and four (4) weeks after normal delivery or unintentional abortion with full pay based on her regular or average weekly wages.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on CIVIL SERVICE AND PROFESSIONAL REGULATION since 2003-02-17

rows.abstract: This measure mandates the Commission on Election (Comelec) to use the Automated Teller Machine (ATM) technology in the conduct of electoral exercises. The system shall involve the use of a voter's card containing the voter's PIN number and an automated machine equipped with a biometric identification system which shall further determine the identity of the voter. The voter's card shall be inserted or otherwise introduced in an appropriate manner into the machine, after which the voter electronically registers his vote. A printed copy of such transaction shall immediately be generated by the machine, which the voter signs. rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE RETENTION OF PHILIPPINE CITIZENSHIP BY NATURAL-BORN FILIPINO CITIZENS WHO ACQUIRE FOREIGN CITIZENSHIP, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE COMMONWEALTH ACT NO. 63, AS AMENDED, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSE
rows.abstract: This bill seeks to allow natural-born citizens of the Philippines, who have lost their citizenship by naturalization in foreign country, to retain their Filipino citizenship with a condition that they register their intent to retain their Filipino citizenship and to manifest their loyalty and allegiance to the Republic of the Philippines, without renouncing their foreign citizenship, with the Bureau of Immigration. Likewise, the bill provides that these Filipino expatriates who qualify for dualcitizenship, shall be granted the same status, right, privileges and responsibilitie s as Filipino citizens and with full civil and political rights.

rows.abstract: This Philippine Occupational Safety and Health Code of 2003." rows.status: Pending with the Committee on HEALTH since 2003-03-03

rows.author: C130
rows.title_full: AN ACT TO ENSURE PUBLIC ACCESS TO OFFICIAL INFORMATION AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: "The Right to Information Act of 2003." Rationale: The people's right to official information is not only a political imperative. It is also essential in economic life. A free flow of official information results in better government polices. It provides the institutional foundation for a more responsive government planning by enhancing the capacity of the public to provide timely feedback to government. The availability of official information widens the base for the generation of more knowledge about key development issues, not only by researchers and academic institutions, but also by the public at large. > This Act, therefore, seeks to (a) put in place a uniform, simple, speedy and effective means of enforcing the right to information;; (b) provide a clear penalty for the unlawful denial of access to official information; and (c) clarify further the scope of the guarantee by defining its coverage.
rows.status: Substituted by HB06671

rows.status: Substituted by HB06670

rows.abstract: "National Police Commission Act of 2003." As proposed in this Act, NAPOLCOM shall be placed under the Office of the President, composed of a Chairperson with a rank equivalent to a Cabinet Secretary and four regular commissioners, each with a rank equivalent to an Undersecretary. > NAPOLCOM shall take charge of police operations involving public safety, administer affairs concerning police education, police communication, criminal identification, criminal statistics and police equipment, and coordinate matters realted to police administration.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on GOVERNMENT REORGANIZATION since 2003-03-05

rows.abstract: "Pilotage Service Act of 2002." It is the purpose of this proposed measure to institutionaliz e prevailing practices in pilotage services, to rationalize the Pilotage fees and other charges related to the pilotage services such as tug assistance andovertime work during nighttme and Sundays and Holidays, to define the legal relations between the harbor pilots, and pilotage organizations in a particular pilotage district with the Harbor Authorities for specific parts already established or thatmay be established from time to time by Congressional Act.

rows.title_full: AN ACT CREATING A COFFEE RESEARCH , DEVELOPMENT AND EXTENSION CENTER, APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: This bill seeks to create a Coffee Research, Development and Extension Center (CoRDEC) that shall be tasked to educate and train all stakeholders of the cofee industry, conduct relevant researches, scientific study and feasible marketing strategies,extend technologices and develop and maintain linkages with international organizations and other coffee development center in other countries. > The Center shall enjoy exemption from taxes and other duties in the importation of such machineries necessary for the development of and extension programs subjected to the provisions of Section 105 (s) of the Tariff and Customs Code, Section 103 (f) of the National Internal Revenue code and to the provisions on Automatic Appropriations under the Geneeral Appropriations Act.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on HIGHER AND TECHNICAL EDUCATION since 2003-03-05
